note: ffprobe read each file independently of the pipeline; a run with no reading here is a file that was written and could not be parsed, which the integrity gate treats as a failure rather than as an absent row. codecs_seen is aggregated off each record's `codec` field - the field ffprobe_validate writes - and a record with no codec there is listed under rows_without_a_codec instead of becoming a null in the set of names. The frame count is `packets` against each record's own `expected_frames`, and width, height and fps are re-read against the expectation block of the execution that wrote the record, so a gate here never rests on a boolean that nobody checked against the numbers beside it
